claims.text: Integrating ultrafast pulsed laser processing with in-situ powder-bed preheating reduces thermal gradients during additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi mini-components.
Reduced processing thermal gradients lower residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi mini-components.
The combined intervention improves mechanical properties relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing causes significant residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing degrades the microstructural integrity of AlCrFeNiSi components.
A reduced thermal gradient promotes more uniform solidification.
More uniform solidification produces refined grain structures.
Reducing the thermal gradient mitigates residual-stress accumulation.
Powder-bed preheating reduces the temperature differential between molten and surrounding material.
Ultrafast pulsed laser processing minimizes dwell time at extreme temperatures.
Combining preheating with ultrafast pulsed laser processing diminishes rapid thermal cycling.
Diminished rapid thermal cycling lowers thermal shock and associated stress buildup.
The proposed process produces a more homogeneous microstructure than conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The proposed process improves hardness and tensile strength relative to conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Conventional high-energy laser powder-bed fusion inevitably generates steep thermal gradients.
Maintaining uniform powder-bed preheating is more challenging for larger components than for miniature components.
The magnitude of stress reduction and property enhancement depends on laser pulse duration, laser energy, and preheating temperature.
